```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sentimentr)
library(lubridate)
library(magrittr)
```

# Import my data

My file has one row per line of text, so I first put each article's lines back together into one row per article.

```{r}
articles_df <- read_csv("articles_df.csv")

articles <- articles_df |> 
  filter(!is.na(sentence)) |> 
  group_by(filename) |> 
  summarize(published_date = first(published_date),
            text = paste(sentence, collapse = " ")) |> 
  mutate(year = year(as.Date(published_date))) |> 
  mutate(id = row_number()) |> 
  select(id, year, text)

nrow(articles)   # number of articles
head(articles)
```

# Part 1: Sentiment for all articles

```{r}
articles_sentiment <- articles |> 
  select(id, text) |> 
  get_sentences() |> 
  sentiment_by(by = c("id"))

# add the scores back to my articles
articles <- articles |> 
  left_join(as_tibble(articles_sentiment) |> select(id, ave_sentiment), by = "id")
```

```{r}
articles |> 
  summarize(min = min(ave_sentiment),
            max = max(ave_sentiment),
            median = median(ave_sentiment),
            sd = sd(ave_sentiment))
```

```{r}
print(paste0("The most positive article was scored at ", max(articles$ave_sentiment),
             " while the most negative was scored at ", min(articles$ave_sentiment),
             ". For context, the median value was ", median(articles$ave_sentiment), "."))
```

# Part 2: Recent vs. older

Use summarize() to see how many articles there are in each year, to pick a cutoff.

```{r}
articles |> 
  group_by(year) |> 
  summarize(number_of_articles = n(),
            average_sentiment = mean(ave_sentiment))
```

Most of my articles are from 2021, and 2026 has only one article, so I chose 2022 as the cutoff. (Change this number if you choose a different year.)

```{r}
cutoff <- 2022

recent <- articles |> filter(year >= cutoff)
older  <- articles |> filter(year < cutoff)
```

## Recent years

```{r}
recent_sentiment <- recent |> 
  select(id, text) |> 
  get_sentences() |> 
  sentiment_by(by = c("id"))

as_tibble(recent_sentiment) |> 
  summarize(min = min(ave_sentiment),
            max = max(ave_sentiment),
            median = median(ave_sentiment),
            sd = sd(ave_sentiment))
```

## Older years

```{r}
older_sentiment <- older |> 
  select(id, text) |> 
  get_sentences() |> 
  sentiment_by(by = c("id"))

as_tibble(older_sentiment) |> 
  summarize(min = min(ave_sentiment),
            max = max(ave_sentiment),
            median = median(ave_sentiment),
            sd = sd(ave_sentiment))
```

# Part 3: Highlighter

This highlights positive and negative sentences in all of my text. It opens in your web browser and also saves as polarity.html in your project folder.

```{r}
articles |> 
  mutate(review = get_sentences(text)) %$%
  sentiment_by(review, id) %>%
  highlight(file = "polarity.html")
```

# Part 4: Emotion

```{r}
articles_emotion <- articles |> 
  select(id, text) |> 
  get_sentences() |> 
  emotion()

head(articles_emotion)
```

Average emotion score by emotion type (I removed the "negated" ones, like "not happy").

```{r}
emotion_summary <- articles_emotion |> 
  filter(!str_detect(emotion_type, "negated")) |> 
  group_by(emotion_type) |> 
  summarize(average_emotion = mean(emotion)) |> 
  arrange(desc(average_emotion))

emotion_summary
```

```{r}
ggplot(emotion_summary, aes(x = reorder(emotion_type, average_emotion), y = average_emotion)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Emotion", y = "Average emotion score")
```
